title.en: Altamira’s bison painters work the cave ceiling by lamp-flame
title.zh: 阿尔塔米拉画师借石灯微光在洞顶绘野牛

location.label: Cave of Altamira, Cantabria, northern Spain

labelI18n.en: Cave of Altamira, Cantabria, northern Spain
labelI18n.zh: 西班牙北部坎塔布里亚阿尔塔米拉洞穴

summary.en:
Crouching beneath a low limestone ceiling near the Bay of Biscay, Magdalenian artists ground red and yellow iron oxides with charcoal and water, then fitted curled steppe bison onto the natural bosses of the rock. Where a stone bulge swelled outward, a shoulder or flank took three-dimensional volume under flickering marrow-fat lamps. Engraved outlines cut with flint burins sharpened horns, hooves and watching eyes.

For generations before a rockfall sealed the entrance around 13,000 years ago, hunter-gatherers camped in the sunlit mouth of Altamira while reserving the dark inner chambers for painting and engraving. While Jōmon communities on the far side of Eurasia were firing their earliest cord-marked cooking pots, Cantabrian bands turned mineral pigment and cave relief into a shared visual memory of Ice Age herds.
summary.zh:
在比斯开湾附近的低矮石灰岩洞顶下，马格德林文化的画师将红黄铁矿石颜料与木炭研磨调水，顺着岩石天然凸起的瘤体绘出蜷卧的草原野牛。石壁隆起处恰好化作牛肩与腹胁，在骨髓油脂石灯摇曳的火光下显出立体起伏；燧石刻刀刮出的细线则勾勒出牛角、蹄尖与凝视的双眼。

在距今约一万三千年前洞口崩塌封闭之前，采集狩猎人群世代在向阳的洞口营地生火栖居，而幽暗的深处洞室则留给彩绘与石刻。当欧亚大陆另一端的绳文社群开始烧制最早的煮食陶器时，坎塔布里亚的猎人正用矿物颜料与岩壁浮凸记录冰期兽群的共同记忆。

dateNote.en: Focused on the late Magdalenian polychrome ceiling phase, roughly 13,000–12,000 BCE (c. 15,000–14,000 BP); earlier cave occupation began millennia sooner.
dateNote.zh: 聚焦于马格德林晚期多色洞顶壁画阶段，约公元前13000—前12000年；洞穴更早的人类活动可追溯至数千年前。

title.en: Monte Verde’s peat bog preserves tents, seaweeds and a child’s footprint
title.zh: 蒙特维德泥炭沼封存木构帐篷、海藻与孩童脚印

location.label: Monte Verde (Chinchihuapi Creek), Los Lagos, southern Chile

labelI18n.en: Monte Verde (Chinchihuapi Creek), Los Lagos, southern Chile
labelI18n.zh: 智利南部湖大区钦奇瓦皮溪畔蒙特维德遗址

summary.en:
Along a small creek in cool, forested southern Chile, families drove split timber stakes into damp ground, lashed wooden frames with reed cordage, and draped animal hides overhead to break the southern wind. Soon after they left, rising water laid an oxygen-poor peat blanket over the camp, preserving wood, knotted string, chewed cuds of Pacific seaweed, wild potatoes and a single child’s footprint pressed beside a hearth.

Nine species of marine algae carried from beaches and estuaries dozens of kilometres away supplied iodine, salt and medicine alongside gomphothere meat and Temperate rainforest tubers. Dating to roughly 14,500 years ago, Monte Verde overturned the long-held assumption that people entered the Americas only much later behind Clovis spear-makers on the North American plains.
summary.zh:
在智利南部清冷湿润的林间溪畔，数户人家将劈开的木桩打入湿地，用芦苇绳索捆扎木架、披覆兽皮以抵御南风。营地废弃后不久，上涨的水位覆上一层缺氧泥炭，奇迹般封存了木桩、绳结、嚼过的太平洋海藻团、野生马铃薯残迹，以及火塘旁一枚清晰的孩童脚印。

从数十公里外的海滩与河口采来的九种海藻，为营地提供了碘、盐分与药材，与嵌齿象肉和温带雨林块茎共同构成食谱。蒙特维德距今约一万四千五百年的年代，打破了学界长期认为人类须待北美克洛维斯猎人之后才进入美洲的旧说。

dateNote.en: Calibrated radiocarbon dates for Monte Verde II cluster around 14,550–14,000 cal BP (shown as c. 12,500–11,800 BCE).
dateNote.zh: 蒙特维德二期校正碳十四年代集中于距今约14550—14000年（此处标为约公元前12500—前11800年）。

title.en: Builders beside Jericho’s spring raise a stone tower and staircase
title.zh: 耶利哥泉畔居民筑起石塔与内旋石阶

location.label: Tell es-Sultan (ancient Jericho), Jordan Valley, Palestine

labelI18n.en: Tell es-Sultan (ancient Jericho), Jordan Valley, Palestine
labelI18n.zh: 约旦河谷泰尔苏丹遗址（古耶利哥）

summary.en:
Long before anyone in the Levant fired clay pots or smelted metal, residents clustered around the perennial Ein es-Sultan spring hauled undressed boulders to build a perimeter wall, a rock-cut ditch and an 8.5-metre conical stone tower. Inside the tower’s dark core, twenty-two hammered stone steps still climb to a top platform looking across the Jordan Valley oasis and the western hills.

Whether engineered to deflect flash floods, mark solstice shadows from Mount Quruntul or project communal authority, the work demanded coordinated labour across scores of mudbrick households. Beneath house floors in the succeeding Pre-Pottery Neolithic phase, families buried relatives and modelled fine lime plaster over selected skulls with cowrie-shell eyes—anchoring lineage and memory directly into domestic space.
summary.zh:
在黎凡特尚未出现陶器与冶金的年代，聚居在艾因苏丹常流泉畔的居民搬运未经雕琢的巨石，筑起围墙、凿岩壕沟与一座高约8.5米的圆锥形石塔。幽暗的塔身内部嵌着二十二级石阶，至今仍可拾级登上俯瞰约旦河谷绿洲与西侧山峦的塔顶平台。

无论它旨在阻挡山洪泥流、呼应库伦图尔山的夏至日影，还是彰显聚落共同体的凝聚力，这项工程都意味着数十座泥砖居址之间的协力劳作。在随后的前陶新石器阶段，居民将亲人葬于屋内地面之下，并以细腻石灰膏在部分头骨上塑出面容、镶入货贝作眼，使家族记忆与居所融为一体。

dateNote.en: Spans the Pre-Pottery Neolithic A stone tower and wall (~8300–7800 BCE) into the Pre-Pottery Neolithic B plastered-skull households (~7800–7300 BCE).
dateNote.zh: 涵盖前陶新石器A期石塔与围墙（约公元前8300—前7800年）及前陶新石器B期塑面头骨居址阶段（约公元前7800—前7300年）。

title.en: Green Sahara cattle herders align solstice stones at Nabta Playa
title.zh: 绿撒哈拉牧牛人在纳布塔普拉亚立起夏至石阵

location.label: Nabta Playa basin, Nubian Desert, southern Egypt

labelI18n.en: Nabta Playa basin, Nubian Desert, southern Egypt
labelI18n.zh: 埃及南部努比亚沙漠纳布塔普拉亚盆地

summary.en:
Today hyper-arid desert west of Abu Simbel, Nabta Playa once filled with summer monsoon rains during the African Humid Period, drawing gazelle, hares and mobile pastoralists driving herds of cattle. Families dug deep walk-in wells to survive dry months, harvested wild sorghum across the basin floor and decorated early pottery with dotted wavy lines.

As the monsoon grew erratic in the fifth millennium BCE, pastoral bands gathered at the lake edge for seasonal ceremonies, burying whole young cattle in clay-lined chambers roofed with tamarisk logs and setting a small ring of sandstone slabs with sightlines opening toward the summer solstice sunrise—the sky signal that promised returning rain. When the desert dried further, those herding and astronomical traditions moved east toward the Nile Valley.
summary.zh:
今日阿布辛贝以西极度干旱的纳布塔普拉亚盆地，在非洲湿润期曾因夏季季风降雨汇成季节性湖泊，吸引瞪羚、野兔与赶着牛群迁徙的牧人。人们开凿可步入汲水的深井度过旱季，采集盆地中的野生高粱，并在早期陶器上压印出点状波浪纹。

公元前五千纪季风渐趋不稳时，各支牧群在湖畔举行季节性集会，把整头幼牛葬入柽柳原木封顶的泥衬墓室，并竖起一圈砂岩板石，留出指向夏至日出的观测缺口——那是预示雨季重临的天象信号。随着撒哈拉再度干涸，这些畜牧与观象传统向东汇入尼罗河谷。

dateNote.en: Covers Holocene lake-basin occupation from early well-digging and ceramics (~7500 BCE) through cattle tumuli and stone alignments (~4800 BCE).
dateNote.zh: 涵盖全新世湖盆聚居期，自早期凿井与制陶（约公元前7500年）延续至牛葬冢与砂岩石阵阶段（约公元前4800年）。

sources.publisher: Combined Prehistoric Expedition / Institute of Archaeology and Ethnology, Polish Academy of Sciences
sources.evidenceNote: Primary archaeological monograph documenting Holocene playa stratigraphy, deep wells, sorghum storage pits, cattle burials, and Late Neolithic megalithic alignments.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 联合史前考察队考古专著，记录全新世季节湖地层、深井、高粱窖穴、牛祭葬及新石器晚期巨石排列。

sources.evidenceNote: Summarizes paleolake hydrology during the African Humid Period and the summer-solstice orientation of the reconstructed stone circle now at Aswan’s Nubian Museum.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 概述非洲湿润期古湖泊水文环境及现迁建于阿斯旺努比亚博物馆的夏至定向石圈。

reviewLimit.en: Summer-solstice sightlines in the stone circle are well documented, whereas more elaborate stellar claims for surrounding stone clusters remain contested.
reviewLimit.zh: 石圈的夏至日出观测线有扎实的测绘依据，而关于周边石群对应复杂恒星坐标的假说在学界仍有争议。

title.en: Jiahu villagers carve playable crane-bone flutes and brew rice wine
title.zh: 贾湖先民以丹顶鹤尺骨琢笛并酿造稻米蜜酒

location.label: Jiahu site, Wuyang County, Henan, central China

labelI18n.en: Jiahu site, Wuyang County, Henan, central China
labelI18n.zh: 中国河南舞阳县贾湖遗址

summary.en:
Between marshes and slow rivers on the southern Huai plain, Neolithic villagers at Jiahu harvested wetland rice, trapped fish and waterfowl, and selected the hollow wing bones (ulnae) of red-crowned cranes to fashion more than thirty end-blown flutes. Before drilling five to eight finger holes, instrument makers scored layout marks along the bone—and on one seven-hole flute dated around 6000 BCE, added a tiny tuning hole beside the seventh aperture so it could sound a clear scale.

Chemical residues inside Jiahu’s pointed-bottom pottery jars revealed another craft of gathering and hospitality: the earliest chemically attested fermented beverage, brewed from rice, wild grape or hawthorn fruit, and honeywax. Engraved tortoise shells placed in graves hint at divination practices millennia before Shang oracle bones.
summary.zh:
在淮河上游支流与沼泽交织的平原上，贾湖村落的居民收割湿地稻谷、捕捞鱼鳖水禽，并挑选丹顶鹤中空的尺骨，琢磨出三十余支竖吹骨笛。匠人在钻出五至八个音孔之前，先在骨管表面刻下定位线；一支约公元前6000年的七孔骨笛还在第七孔旁补钻细小调音孔，至今仍能吹奏出清亮音阶。

尖底陶罐内壁的化学残留物揭示了聚饮与款待的另一门手艺：用稻米、山楂或野生葡萄配以蜂蜜酿成的发酵酒液。部分墓葬随葬的刻符龟甲，也在商代甲骨文出现数千年前留下了占卜仪式的线索。

dateNote.en: Radiocarbon dates across three Jiahu occupation phases span roughly 7000–5700 BCE.
dateNote.zh: 贾湖遗址三期文化层的碳十四测年跨度约为公元前7000—前5700年。

sources.evidenceNote: Documents excavation of >30 red-crowned crane ulna flutes across 7000–5700 BCE strata, layout scratch marks, tuning hole, and acoustic testing.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 记录公元前7000—前5700年地层出土的三十余支丹顶鹤尺骨笛、刻划定位线、调音孔及测音结果。

reviewLimit.en: Incised marks on Jiahu tortoise shells show deliberate sign-making, though most scholars treat them as ritual symbols rather than a full writing system.
reviewLimit.zh: 贾湖龟甲刻符体现了有意识的符号刻划，但多数学者将其视为仪式符号，而非成熟的文字系统。

title.en: Mehrgarh farmers build mudbrick granaries and drill living teeth
title.zh: 梅赫尔格尔农人筑泥砖粮仓并以燧石弓钻治牙

location.label: Mehrgarh, Kachi Plain near the Bolan Pass, Balochistan, Pakistan

labelI18n.en: Mehrgarh, Kachi Plain near the Bolan Pass, Balochistan, Pakistan
labelI18n.zh: 巴基斯坦俾路支省博兰山口旁卡奇平原梅赫尔格尔遗址

summary.en:
At the foot of the Bolan Pass linking the Iranian plateau to the Indus plain, early farming households at Mehrgarh built multi-roomed mudbrick houses and compartmented storage granaries packed with six-row barley and einkorn wheat. Even in its aceramic phase around 7000 BCE, graves held turquoise from Central Asia, lapis lazuli from Badakhshan and marine shells from the Arabian Sea—proof that village life grew inside long mountain-and-coast exchange corridors.

Bead-makers soon repurposed their flint-tipped bow drills for human care: eleven molars from nine adults buried in Mehrgarh’s Neolithic cemetery show tiny, concentric drill cavities smoothed again by chewing, recording the earliest known dentistry on living patients millennia before Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.
summary.zh:
在连接伊朗高原与印度河平原的博兰山口脚下，梅赫尔格尔的早期农耕家庭筑起多间泥砖房与分格粮仓，贮存六棱大麦与一粒小麦。即便在约公元前7000年的无陶阶段，墓葬中已随葬中亚绿松石、巴达赫尚青金石与阿拉伯海贝壳，表明定居村落一开始便嵌在跨越山地与海岸的交换走廊之中。

珠饰匠人还将装有燧石钻头的弓钻用于疗愈病痛：新石器墓地中九名成年人的十一颗臼齿留有布满同心旋纹的微小钻孔，孔缘又因生前继续咀嚼而磨圆，在哈拉帕与摩亨佐-达罗兴起数千年前留下了已知最早的活体牙科治疗实证。

dateNote.en: Focuses on Mehrgarh Period I (aceramic Neolithic, c. 7000–5500 BCE), when mudbrick granaries, long-distance bead exchange, and flint bow-drill dentistry appear.
dateNote.zh: 聚焦梅赫尔格尔一期（无陶新石器时代，约公元前7000—前5500年），涵盖泥砖粮仓、远距珠饰交换与燧石弓钻治牙遗存。

sources.evidenceNoteZh: 记载博兰山口卡奇平原位置、无陶期泥砖房屋与分格粮仓、大麦小麦种植及远距海贝青金石随葬品；属预备名录文本。

sources.evidenceNoteZh: 同行评审扫描电镜分析确认距今7500—9000年新石器时代梅赫尔格尔九名成人十一颗活体钻孔臼齿由燧石钻头钻治。

reviewLimit.zh: 梅赫尔格尔聚落一直延续至约公元前2500年；本条聚焦其最早的新石器农耕、远距交换与工艺层位。

title.en: Varna’s Black Sea smiths hammer the world’s earliest gold regalia
title.zh: 瓦尔纳黑海金匠锻造世界最早的黄金权杖与礼饰

location.label: Varna Chalcolithic Necropolis, Black Sea coast, Bulgaria

labelI18n.en: Varna Chalcolithic Necropolis, Black Sea coast, Bulgaria
labelI18n.zh: 保加利亚黑海沿岸瓦尔纳铜石并用时代墓地

summary.en:
Near a coastal lake opening onto the western Black Sea, fifth-millennium BCE metallurgists channeled Balkan copper ores, Aegean Spondylus shell and alluvial gold into shimmering markers of rank. Across nearly three hundred Chalcolithic graves at Varna, archaeologists uncovered more than 3,000 gold objects weighing over six kilograms—beaded necklaces, bull-shaped appliqués, bracelets and gold-sheathed axe-sceptres.

Strikingly, several of the richest graves held no human skeleton at all: instead, life-sized clay masks were adorned with gold diadems, earstuds and mouth-plates as cenotaphs for revered powers or absent leaders. In Grave 43, a tall man in his forties went into the earth holding a gold-mounted sceptre alongside nearly a thousand separate gold ornaments, centuries before royal goldsmithing appeared in Egypt or Mesopotamia.
summary.zh:
在通向黑海西岸的滨海湖畔，公元前五千纪的冶金匠人汇聚巴尔干铜矿、爱琴海棘牡蛎壳与砂金，锻打出炫目的等级徽记。在瓦尔纳近三百座铜石并用时代墓葬中，考古学家发掘出三千余件、总重逾六千克的黄金器物——金珠项饰、公牛形金片、金镯以及包金石斧权杖。

引人注目的是，数座随葬品最丰厚的墓穴并无遗骸，而是在等身泥塑面具上缀以金冠、耳饰与护口金片，作为象征权威或纪念远逝首领的空冢。在第43号墓中，一名四十余岁的高大男子手握包金权杖下葬，身畔环绕近千件金饰，比埃及与美索不达米亚的王室金器早了数百年。

dateNote.en: AMS radiocarbon dates place the Varna I Chalcolithic cemetery between roughly 4600 and 4200 BCE.
dateNote.zh: 加速器质谱碳十四测年将瓦尔纳铜石并用时代墓地定于约公元前4600—前4200年。

sources.evidenceNote: Establishes the mid-fifth millennium BCE AMS radiocarbon chronology (~4560–4450 BCE core) and extreme wealth differentiation across Grave 43 and cenotaph burials.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 确立公元前五千纪中叶（核心期约公元前4560—前4450年）加速器碳十四年代，并分析第43号墓与象征性空冢展现的显著社会分化。

sources.publisher: Geologica Balcanica, Bulgarian Academy of Sciences
sources.evidenceNote: Documents >3,000 gold artifacts (~6 kg total), Balkan copper/gold provenance, clay mask cenotaphs, and Varna Archaeological Museum holdings.

expansion.sourceReview: Reviewed against Higham et al. (Antiquity) AMS dating and Bulgarian Academy of Sciences metallographic documentation.

reviewLimit.en: Varna’s cemetery survived far better than its adjacent lakeside settlement, so ritual hierarchy is clearer than daily household organization.
reviewLimit.zh: 瓦尔纳墓地的保存状况远优于邻近湖畔居址，因此丧葬礼仪等级比日常家户组织更为清晰。

title.en: Fisher-foragers raise Watson Brake’s eleven-mound oval ridge
title.zh: 渔猎采集者在沃森布雷克筑起十一座土墩环垄

location.label: Watson Brake, Ouachita River terrace, northern Louisiana, USA

labelI18n.en: Watson Brake, Ouachita River terrace, northern Louisiana, USA
labelI18n.zh: 美国路易斯安那州北部沃希托河阶地沃森布雷克遗址

summary.en:
Nearly two thousand years before Poverty Point and a millennium before Egypt’s first pyramids, seasonal fisher-foragers on a bluff overlooking the Ouachita River wetlands carried basketload after basketload of earth to raise eleven mounds linked by an oval ridge 280 metres across. The tallest mound rose more than seven metres above the terrace—built by communities who grew no maize, made no pottery and answered to no hereditary king.

Charred bones and seeds left between building layers show families feasting from summer into autumn on freshwater drum, catfish, mussels, turtle, deer and wildlambsquarters, while firing small clay blocks to boil food in skin or basket containers. Watson Brake proved that monumental architecture in North America began through cooperative seasonal gatherings of mobile wetland peoples.
summary.zh:
在波弗蒂角兴起近两千年前、埃及最早金字塔动工约一千年前，聚集在沃希托河湿地高岸上的季节性渔猎采集人群一筐接一筐搬运泥土，筑起由直径约280米的椭圆形土垄相连的十一座土墩。最高的主墩隆起逾七米——而建造者既不种玉米、不烧陶器，也没有世袭君王。

筑土层之间的烧骨与炭化种子显示，人们每逢夏秋在此聚会，捕食淡水石首鱼、鲶鱼、河蚌、水龟与白尾鹿，采集藜属野籽，并烧热小泥块投入兽皮或编篮容器中煮食。沃森布雷克证明，北美大陆的大型纪念性建筑始于流动湿地社群自发协作的季节性盛会。

dateNote.en: Radiocarbon dates from mound construction stages span roughly 3500–3000 BCE (Middle Archaic period).
dateNote.zh: 土墩营建各阶段的碳十四测年跨度约为公元前3500—前3000年（北美中古风时期）。

sources.title: A Mound Complex in Louisiana at 5400–5000 Years Before the Present
sources.publisher: Joe W. Saunders et al., Science 277 (1997) / University of Southern Mississippi
sources.evidenceNote: Primary excavation report establishing c. 3500–3000 BCE radiocarbon dates, 11-mound 280-metre oval layout, aquatic/wetland subsistence, fired-clay cooking objects, and pre-agricultural context.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 原始发掘报告确立约公元前3500—前3000年碳十四年代、直径280米十一墩椭圆布局、湿地水生食谱、烧土烹饪块及前农业社会背景。

sources.title: Moundbuilders of the Mississippi Basin — Middle Archaic Earthworks
sources.publisher: National Park Service, U.S. Department of the Interior
sources.evidenceNote: Places Watson Brake within Lower Mississippi Valley Middle Archaic earthwork traditions preceding Poverty Point.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 将沃森布雷克置于早于波弗蒂角的密西西比河下游中古风时期筑墩传统之中。

expansion.sourceReview: Reviewed against Saunders et al. (Science 1997) excavation report and National Park Service Lower Mississippi Valley synthesis.

reviewLimit.en: Because no burials or permanent house floors were excavated inside the enclosure, the exact ceremonies conducted atop the mounds remain open.
reviewLimit.zh: 由于环垄内未发掘出墓葬或永久性房址地面，墩顶所行仪式的具体形式仍待考证。

title.en: Zubayda bint Jaʿfar: engineering water across the Arabian desert
title.zh: 祖拜达：在阿拉伯荒漠开凿朝觐水道的阿拔斯王后

location.label: Mecca terminus of Ayn Zubayda aqueduct, Hejaz

labelI18n.en: Mecca terminus of Ayn Zubayda aqueduct, Hejaz
labelI18n.zh: 希贾兹麦加“祖拜达泉”引水渠终点

summary.en:
Granddaughter of Baghdad’s founder al-Mansur and consort of Caliph Harun al-Rashid, Zubayda bint Jaʿfar turned personal wealth into the largest hydraulic public-works corridor of the early Islamic world. Seeing pilgrims and residents parched during droughts in Mecca and along the 1,400-kilometre Kufa-to-Mecca desert road, she hired surveyors and stonemasons rather than leaving only courtly charity.

When her treasurers warned of the staggering cost of cutting underground qanats and plaster-lined aqueducts from Wadi Nuʿman and Hunayn through solid rock to Mount Arafat and Mecca, biographers record her reply that she would build it ‘even if every pickaxe blow costs a dinar.’ Step-cisterns, milestones, beacon towers and the halfway desert town of Fayd along what became known as Darb Zubayda sustained travellers, merchants and scholars for centuries.
summary.zh:
作为巴格达建城者曼苏尔的孙女、哈里发哈伦·拉希德的妻子，祖拜达·宾特·贾法尔将巨额私产化作早期伊斯兰世界规模最大的公共水利走廊。亲历麦加旱情并目睹库法至麦加一千四百公里沙漠旅途上的焦渴后，她没有止步于宫廷施舍，而是召集测绘师与石匠动工治水。

当账房警告从努尔曼谷地与胡奈因凿岩引水至阿拉法特山和麦加耗资惊人时，史家记载她答道：“哪怕每一镐花费一枚第纳尔也要修成。”沿途修筑的阶梯蓄水池、里程碑、烽火导标以及中点驿城费德，使这条后来以她命名的“祖拜达古道”世代滋养往来行旅、商队与学者。

dateNote.en: c. 766–831 CE; her repeated pilgrimages and hydraulic commissions peaked between the 790s and 810s.
dateNote.zh: 约766—831年；其多次朝觐与水利营建主要集中于8世纪90年代至9世纪初。

title.en: Marries Harun al-Rashid at Baghdad’s caliphal court
title.zh: 在巴格达宫廷嫁予哈伦·拉希德

description.en: Born into the ruling Abbasid house, Zubayda weds her cousin Harun al-Rashid in Baghdad and builds an independent household administration managing estates and endowments.
description.zh: 出身阿拔斯宗室的祖拜达在巴格达与堂兄哈伦·拉希德成婚，建立起独立管理田产与公益捐赠的府邸账务体系。

location.label: Baghdad, Abbasid capital on the Tigris

labelI18n.en: Baghdad, Abbasid capital on the Tigris
labelI18n.zh: 底格里斯河畔阿拔斯都城巴格达

title.en: Commissions the Ayn Zubayda rock-cut aqueduct to Mecca
title.zh: 主持开凿通往麦加的“祖拜达泉”引水渠

description.en: During pilgrimage to the Hejaz, acute water shortages prompt her to fund subterranean channels and vaulted stone conduits carrying spring water over 25 kilometres from Wadi Nuʿman to Arafat and Mecca.
description.zh: 赴希贾兹朝觐期间目睹严重水荒，遂出资开凿地下暗渠与石拱水道，将努尔曼谷地泉水引流二十五公里以上直抵阿拉法特与麦加。

location.label: Wadi Nuʿman and Arafat aqueduct works near Mecca

labelI18n.en: Wadi Nuʿman and Arafat aqueduct works near Mecca
labelI18n.zh: 麦加近郊努尔曼谷地与阿拉法特引水工程

title.en: Expands reservoirs and waystations at Fayd on Darb Zubayda
title.zh: 扩建“祖拜达古道”中点费德驿城的蓄水池与驿站

description.en: Engineers line dozens of desert stations between Kufa and Mecca with flood-diverting dams, stepped circular birka cisterns, wells and hostels anchored by the oasis hub of Fayd.
description.zh: 工匠在库法至麦加沿线数十处荒漠驿站修筑拦洪坝、圆形阶梯蓄水池、水井与旅舍，并以绿洲重镇费德为中枢。

location.label: Fayd oasis station on Darb Zubayda, northern Arabia

labelI18n.en: Fayd oasis station on Darb Zubayda, northern Arabia
labelI18n.zh: 阿拉伯北部“祖拜达古道”费德绿洲驿城

title.en: Dies in Baghdad as her waterworks endure across reigns
title.zh: 卒于巴格达，所筑水利走廊跨越朝代延续

description.en: Surviving the civil war between her son al-Amin and stepson al-Maʾmun, Zubayda dies in Baghdad in 831 while travellers from Iraq and Persia continue drawing water from her cisterns.
description.zh: 历经儿子阿明与继子马蒙之间的内战后，祖拜达于831年在巴格达去世，而往来伊拉克与波斯的行人仍世代汲用她修筑的水池。

labelI18n.zh: 伊拉克巴格达

title.en: Benjamin of Tudela: counting communities from Navarre to Baghdad
title.zh: 图德拉的本雅明：从纳瓦拉到巴格达记录犹太社群与商港

location.label: Tudela on the Ebro River, Kingdom of Navarre, Spain

labelI18n.en: Tudela on the Ebro River, Kingdom of Navarre, Spain
labelI18n.zh: 西班牙纳瓦拉王国埃布罗河畔图德拉

summary.en:
A century before Marco Polo set out from Venice, Benjamin ben Jonah left the Ebro River town of Tudela in Navarre and spent more than a decade walking and sailing across roughly three hundred cities in southern Europe, Byzantium, Crusader Syria, Mesopotamia and Fatimid-to-Ayyubid Egypt. Writing in clear, observant Hebrew, he recorded headcounts of local Jewish scholars and households alongside dyers, glassmakers, spice markets and harbour tolls.

In Constantinople he marvelled at merchants arriving from Rus’, Lombardy and Baghdad and watched chariot games in the Hippodrome; in Abbasid Baghdad he described hospitals caring for patients at public expense; in Alexandria he counted commercial fondacos for twenty-eight Christian and Muslim realms. His *Sefer ha-Masaʿot* reveals a twelfth-century Mediterranean and Indian Ocean hinge bound together by everyday trade despite crusading wars.
summary.zh:
在马可·波罗自威尼斯启程一个世纪之前，约拿之子本雅明离开纳瓦拉王国埃布罗河畔的图德拉，历时十余年水陆兼程，走访南欧、拜占庭、十字军叙利亚、两河流域与埃及的约三百座城镇。他以简明敏锐的希伯来文记下各地犹太学者与家户人数，也记录染匠、玻璃工匠、香料集市与港口税银。

在君士坦丁堡，他惊叹于来自罗斯、伦巴第与巴格达的商贾云集，并观看赛马场的竞技；在阿拔斯都城巴格达，他描绘公费收治病患的医院；在亚历山大港，他清点出分属二十八个基督教与穆斯林政权的商馆。这部《本雅明游记》展现出十二世纪十字军战火之外，由日常贸易紧密织联的地中海与印度洋枢纽世界。

dateNote.en: Focused on his documented Mediterranean and West Asian journey, c. 1159/1165–1173 CE.
dateNote.zh: 聚焦其有据可考的地中海与西亚游历年代，约1159/1165—1173年。

title.en: Departs Tudela down the Ebro toward Mediterranean ports
title.zh: 自图德拉顺埃布罗河南下地中海商港

description.en: Leaving Navarre via Zaragoza, Barcelona and Provençal study centres, Benjamin begins recording scholars, synagogues and merchant networks in each port.
description.zh: 经萨拉戈萨、巴塞罗那与普罗旺斯学术重镇离开纳瓦拉，开始逐城记录学者名录、会堂与商贸网络。

labelI18n.zh: 纳瓦拉王国图德拉

title.en: Observes papal Rome and Italian maritime republics
title.zh: 考察教宗驻地罗马与意大利海商共和国

description.en: Passing Genoa and Pisa’s towered neighbourhoods, he reaches Rome under Pope Alexander III and notes Jewish stewards serving directly in the papal household.
description.zh: 途经塔楼林立的热那亚与比萨抵达教宗亚历山大三世治下的罗马，记下在教廷直接任职管理财务的犹太官员。

labelI18n.zh: 教宗国罗马

title.en: Describes Constantinople’s silk wealth and Pera quarter
title.zh: 记述君士坦丁堡的丝绸财富与佩拉犹太区

description.en: In Manuel I Komnenos’s capital, Benjamin compares Constantinople’s customs revenue solely to Baghdad’s while noting the legal restrictions imposed on silk artisans in Pera.
description.zh: 在曼努埃尔一世治下的帝都，他感叹唯有巴格达可与君士坦丁堡的商税比肩，同时如实记下金角湾对岸佩拉丝织工匠所受的法令限制。

labelI18n.zh: 东罗马帝国君士坦丁堡

title.zh: 探访巴格达哈里发宫廷、经学院与公立医院

description.en: Travelling through Jerusalem, Damascus and Mosul to Baghdad, he portrays the Exilarch Daniel ben Hisdai and the Dar al-Maristan hospital treating the sick from caliphal funds.
description.zh: 经耶路撒冷、大马士革与摩苏尔抵达巴格达，记述流散领袖丹尼尔·本·希斯代及由国库供养病患的医院。

labelI18n.zh: 阿拔斯哈里发国巴格达

title.zh: 在亚历山大港清点二十八国商馆后扬帆西归

title.en: Rabban Bar Sauma: from Beijing to Paris and Rome as Mongol envoy
title.zh: 拉班·扫马：从大都走入巴黎与罗马的景教使节

location.label: Maragheh, Ilkhanid capital in northwestern Iran

labelI18n.en: Maragheh, Ilkhanid capital in northwestern Iran
labelI18n.zh: 伊朗西北部伊儿汗国重镇马拉盖

summary.en:
Born into a prosperous Turkic Ongud Christian family in Khanbaliq (modern Beijing), the ascetic monk Rabban Bar Sauma set out westward around 1275 with his young pupil Markos, hoping only to pray at Jerusalem’s shrines. Crossing the Taklamakan oasis road with a safe-conduct from Kublai Khan, the pair reached Ilkhanid Iran just as warfare blocked the Syrian roads—and watched Markos unexpectedly elected Patriarch Yahballaha III of the Church of the East.

In 1287 the Mongol ruler Arghun Khan chose the multilingual sixty-year-old monk to carry letters across the Black Sea and Mediterranean to Europe’s courts, proposing a joint Mongol–Frankish alliance against Mamluk Egypt. Bar Sauma debated cardinals in Rome, admired Sainte-Chapelle with Philip IV in Paris, received communion from Edward I at Bordeaux, and left a rare East Asian traveller’s eye-view of medieval Europe.
summary.zh:
出生在汗八里（今北京）富裕汪古部基督教家庭的隐修修士拉班·扫马，于1275年前后携年轻弟子马可西行，原本只求赴耶路撒冷圣地礼拜。两人持忽必烈颁授的通行凭证穿越塔克拉玛干绿洲商道抵达伊儿汗国，却因叙利亚战乱受阻；其间弟子马可竟意外获选为东方教会大公雅巴拉哈三世。

1287年，蒙古伊儿汗阿鲁浑选派这位年逾花甲、通晓多语的修士横渡黑海与地中海出使欧洲诸廷，提议蒙古与法兰克君主夹击埃及马穆鲁克王朝。扫马在罗马与枢机主教团辩经，在巴黎随腓力四世瞻仰圣礼拜堂，在波尔多领受英王爱德华一世的接待，留下了中世纪极为罕见的自东亚审视西欧的行纪。

dateNote.en: c. 1225–1294 CE; departed Khanbaliq c. 1275–1278 and conducted his European embassy in 1287–1288.

title.en: Leaves Khanbaliq westward with his disciple Markos
title.zh: 携弟子马可自大都启程西行

description.en: After years as a hermit in the hills near Beijing, Bar Sauma departs Kublai Khan’s capital with Markos along the Tangut and Tarim caravan oases.
description.zh: 在北京近郊山中隐修多年后，扫马与弟子马可自忽必烈都城出发，循西夏故地与塔里木绿洲商道西进。

labelI18n.zh: 元代大都（汗八里，今北京）

title.en: Witnesses Markos enthroned as Patriarch in Ilkhanid Iran
title.zh: 在伊儿汗国见证弟子马可升任东方教会大公

description.en: Halted from reaching Jerusalem by Mamluk–Ilkhanid fighting, the travellers settle in Iran, where bishops elect Markos as Catholicos-Patriarch Mar Yahballaha III in 1281.
description.zh: 因马穆鲁克与伊儿汗国交战无法前往耶路撒冷而留驻伊朗；1281年众主教推举马可继任东方教会大公雅巴拉哈三世。

labelI18n.zh: 伊儿汗国马拉盖

title.en: Sails via Constantinople and Naples to debate cardinals in Rome
title.zh: 经君士坦丁堡与那不勒斯抵罗马与枢机团论道

description.en: Sent west by Arghun Khan, Bar Sauma views Hagia Sophia, watches Mount Etna erupt at sea, and arrives in Rome during a papal vacancy to explain Church of the East creed to questioning cardinals.
description.zh: 奉阿鲁浑汗之命西使，途经圣索菲亚大教堂并目睹埃特纳火山喷发，于教宗虚位期抵罗马向枢机主教阐明东方教会信经。

labelI18n.zh: 教宗国罗马

title.en: Meets Philip IV in Paris and Edward I in Gascony
title.zh: 在巴黎会晤法王腓力四世并赴加斯科涅见英王爱德华一世

description.en: In Paris he marvels at the 30,000 scholars of the university and the royal tombs at Saint-Denis, then rides south to Bordeaux where King Edward I welcomes Arghun’s envoy.
description.zh: 在巴黎赞叹大学三万学子之盛并参观圣但尼王陵，随后南下波尔多获英王爱德华一世接见并呈递盟书。

labelI18n.zh: 法兰西王国巴黎

title.en: Returns with papal letters to Iran and dies at Baghdad
title.zh: 携教宗回函返归伊儿汗国并卒于巴格达

description.en: After receiving Pope Nicholas IV’s blessing in 1288, Bar Sauma reports back to Arghun Khan, builds a church at Maragheh, and dies at Baghdad in January 1294.
description.zh: 1288年获新任教宗尼古拉四世祝福后返朝复命，在马拉盖督建教堂，1294年初病逝于巴格达。

labelI18n.zh: 伊儿汗国辖下巴格达

name.zh: 哈桑·瓦赞（利奥·阿非利加努斯）

title.en: al-Ḥasan al-Wazzān: diplomat from Fez and Timbuktu to Renaissance Rome
title.zh: 哈桑·瓦赞：从非斯、廷巴克图走到文艺复兴罗马的外交官

labelI18n.zh: 摩洛哥瓦塔斯王朝非斯（卡鲁因学区）

summary.en:
Born in Granada just after its fall to Castile and Aragon, al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad al-Wazzān grew up in Fez, studied law at al-Qarawiyyin, and crossed the Sahara on diplomatic and commercial missions to Songhai Timbuktu, Gao, Bornu and Cairo. In 1518 Christian corsairs seized his ship near Djerba and presented the learned envoy to the Medici Pope Leo X in Rome, where he was baptized in St Peter’s Basilica as Johannes Leo de Medicis.

Writing in Italian in 1526 while teaching Arabic and collaborating on Hebrew–Arabic–Latin lexicons, he completed his *Cosmographia et geographia de Affrica*—describing Timbuktu’s thriving market in imported manuscript books alongside Fez’s inns, baths and guilds. Using the parable of an ‘amphibious bird’ swimming when taxed by birds and flying when taxed by fish, he navigated survival between worlds before likely returning to North Africa after the 1527 Sack of Rome.
summary.zh:
生于刚落入卡斯蒂利亚与阿拉贡之手的格拉纳达，哈桑·本·穆罕默德·瓦赞随家人迁居非斯，就读于卡鲁因学府，随后多次奉使或随商队穿越撒哈拉，足迹遍及桑海帝国的廷巴克图、加奥、博尔努与开罗。1518年，基督教私掠船在杰尔巴岛附近截获其座船，将这位博学使节献给罗马的美第奇教宗利奥十世；他在圣伯多禄大殿受洗，获名约翰内斯·利奥。

他在罗马讲授阿拉伯语、合编希伯来—阿拉伯—拉丁三语辞书，并于1526年用意大利文写成《非洲志》，详述廷巴克图利润丰厚的手抄本图书贸易与非斯的旅舍、浴场和行会。他借“水陆两栖之鸟”在群鸟征税时潜入水中、群鱼索税时飞向天空的寓言自况身世；1527年罗马浩劫后，他极可能渡海重返北非。

dateNote.en: c. 1494 – c. 1554 CE; captured in 1518, baptized in Rome in 1520, completed his Africa manuscript in 1526.
dateNote.zh: 约1494—约1554年；1518年被俘，1520年在罗马受洗，1526年完成《非洲志》手稿。

title.en: Refugee family resettles from Granada to Fez
title.zh: 随避难家族自格拉纳达迁居摩洛哥非斯

description.en: Leaving post-conquest Granada in early childhood, al-Wazzān grows up in Fez, working as a notary in its hospital while studying at al-Qarawiyyin.
description.zh: 幼年随家人离开易主后的格拉纳达定居非斯，在卡鲁因求学期间曾任医院书记员。

labelI18n.zh: 摩洛哥非斯

title.en: Crosses the Sahara to Songhai Timbuktu under Askia Muhammad
title.zh: 穿越撒哈拉造访阿斯基亚·穆罕默德治下的廷巴克图

description.en: Accompanying his diplomat uncle and later travelling for the Wattasid sultan, he observes Timbuktu’s judges, salt trade and lucrative manuscript market.
description.zh: 随外交官叔父及奉瓦塔斯苏丹之命远行西非，亲见廷巴克图的学者法官、岩盐贸易与兴盛的手抄本书市。

labelI18n.zh: 桑海帝国廷巴克图（今马里）

title.en: Captive scholar baptized by Pope Leo X in Rome
title.zh: 被俘送往罗马并由教宗利奥十世施洗

description.en: Seized at sea returning from Egypt and Constantinople in 1518, he is freed from Castel Sant’Angelo and baptized in January 1520, beginning years of Arabic scholarship in Italy.
description.zh: 1518年自君士坦丁堡与埃及返航途中在海上被俘，后获释出圣天使堡并于1520年1月受洗，在意大利展开阿拉伯学术著述。

labelI18n.zh: 罗马梵蒂冈与圣天使堡

title.en: Completes his Italian manuscript on Africa before leaving Italy
title.zh: 完成意大利文《非洲志》手稿并于浩劫后渡海返归北非

description.en: After finishing his 900-page geography of North and West Africa in March 1526, he leaves Rome around the 1527 imperial sack and is reported by European contemporaries living again in Tunis.
description.zh: 1526年3月写成九百余页的北非与西非地理志手稿；1527年罗马遭帝国军队洗劫前后离意，据同时代学者记载重返突尼斯生活。

labelI18n.zh: 北非突尼斯

title.en: Malik Ambar: from Ethiopian captivity to prime minister of the Deccan
title.zh: 马利克·安巴尔：从埃塞俄比亚奴隶成长为德干高原宰相

location.label: Khadki (later Aurangabad / Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar), Deccan, India

labelI18n.en: Khadki (later Aurangabad / Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar), Deccan, India
labelI18n.zh: 印度德干高原卡德基（后称奥兰加巴德）

summary.en:
Born Chapu around 1548 in Ethiopia’s Kambata highlands, Malik Ambar was enslaved in youth and carried through Red Sea ports and Mocha to Baghdad, where the merchant Mir Qasim educated him in finance and Arabic administration before selling him into the Deccan sultanate of Ahmadnagar. Freed upon the death of his master Chengiz Khan—himself a fellow Habshi (East African) minister—Ambar raised a multi-ethnic force of Habshi and Maratha light cavalry.

For a quarter-century as Peshwa (regent and prime minister) of Ahmadnagar, his fast-moving Bargigir horsemen repeatedly checked the southward armies of the Mughal emperors Akbar and Jahangir, driving a frustrated Jahangir to commission allegorical miniatures showing himself shooting arrows into Ambar’s severed head—something the Mughals never achieved in life. At his new capital of Khadki, Ambar measured arable land directly with peasants and dug the rock-cut Neher-e-Ambari canal that still carries gravity-fed water into the city.
summary.zh:
约1548年生于埃塞俄比亚坎巴塔高地的恰普，少年被卖为奴，经红海商港与摩卡辗转至巴格达。商贾米尔·卡西姆看重其才智，教他阿拉伯文书与理财，后将他带往印度德干的艾哈迈德讷格尔苏丹国。在同为“哈卜希”（东非裔）大臣的主人成吉思汗病逝获释后，马利克·安巴尔组建起融合东非裔骑兵与马拉塔轻骑的劲旅。

在担任艾哈迈德讷格尔摄政宰相（佩什瓦）的四分之一世纪里，他以神出鬼没的袭扰骑兵屡挫莫卧儿皇帝阿克巴与贾汉吉尔的南征大军；束手无策的贾汉吉尔甚至命宫廷画师绘出自己弯弓射穿安巴尔首级的幻想细密画，而在现实战场上莫卧儿终其一生未能俘获他。在新营建的都城卡德基，安巴尔直接丈量田亩核定赋税，并凿通至今仍靠重力自流供水的“安巴尔暗渠”。

dateNote.en: 1548–1626 CE; served as de facto ruler and Peshwa of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate from c. 1600 until his death in May 1626.
dateNote.zh: 1548—1626年；约1600年至1626年5月去世前任艾哈迈德讷格尔苏丹国实际执政宰相。

title.en: Born Chapu in southern Ethiopia before Red Sea enslavement
title.zh: 生于埃塞俄比亚高地，少年被掠经红海贩运

description.en: Born in the Ethiopian highlands (named Chapu), he is captured or sold into the Red Sea trade through Harar and Yemeni Mocha.
description.zh: 生于埃塞俄比亚高地（原名恰普），少年时沦为奴隶，经哈勒尔与也门摩卡港卷入红海与印度洋人口贸易。

labelI18n.zh: 埃塞俄比亚高地哈勒尔商道

title.en: Trained in finance and Arabic administration in Baghdad
title.zh: 在巴格达习得财政账务与阿拉伯行政管理

description.en: Purchased in Baghdad by the merchant Qazi Hussein (Mir Qasim al-Baghdadi), he receives the name Ambar and masters accounting and governance before sailing to India in the early 1570s.
description.zh: 在巴格达被商人米尔·卡西姆购下并获名安巴尔，系统修习文书与财政，于1570年代初随船横渡阿拉伯海赴印度。

labelI18n.zh: 奥斯曼辖下伊拉克巴格达

title.en: Rallies Habshi and Maratha cavalry to save Ahmadnagar from Mughal conquest
title.zh: 整编哈卜希与马拉塔骑兵阻击莫卧儿南征

description.en: After Mughal troops storm Ahmadnagar fort in 1600, freed commander Ambar installs a Nizam Shahi prince and wages mobile guerrilla campaigns that cut Mughal supply lines across the Deccan.
description.zh: 1600年莫卧儿军攻占艾哈迈德讷格尔要塞后，已获自由的安巴尔拥立尼扎姆·沙希宗室，率机动轻骑切断莫卧儿补给线。

labelI18n.zh: 印度德干马哈拉施特拉艾哈迈德讷格尔

title.en: Founds Khadki with rock-cut subterranean canals and land revenue reform
title.zh: 营建新都卡德基，开凿地下引水暗渠并推行田赋新制

description.en: Establishing Khadki as capital in 1610, he constructs the subterranean Neher-e-Ambari aqueduct, introduces measured peasant revenue assessments, and rules undefeated until dying at nearly eighty in 1626.
description.zh: 1610年建都卡德基，主持凿通地下引水工程“安巴尔渠”并改革直接对农田核税的赋役制度，执政至1626年以近八旬高龄善终。

labelI18n.zh: 德干卡德基（奥兰加巴德）与库尔达巴德

title.en: Gabriela Silang: leading the Ilocos highland uprising during a global war
title.zh: 加布里埃拉·锡朗：七年战争浪潮中率部起义的伊洛科斯女将

location.label: Vigan (Ciudad Fernandina), Ilocos Sur, Luzon, Philippines

labelI18n.en: Vigan (Ciudad Fernandina), Ilocos Sur, Luzon, Philippines
labelI18n.zh: 菲律宾吕宋岛南伊洛科斯省维甘古城

summary.en:
When a British East India Company fleet sailed from Madras during the Seven Years’ War and occupied Spanish Manila in October 1762, colonial authority cracked across northern Luzon. In Ilocos, courier leader Diego Silang and his wife María Josefa Gabriela Cariño—born in Santa to a Spanish-Ilocano father and an Itneg (Tinguian) mother—expelled abusive provincial officials, abolished forced labour (*polo*) and heavy tribute, and set up a free municipal government at Vigan.

After church and royalist plotters paid Diego’s friend Miguel Vicos to assassinate him in May 1763, thirty-two-year-old Gabriela refused to surrender. Riding into the Abra river highlands of her mother’s Itneg kin at Pidigan, she rallied upland archers and lowland horsemen, marched back down to besiege Vigan in September 1763, and met capture and execution alongside dozens of followers without yielding.
summary.zh:
当七年战争的战火从欧洲与北美延烧至亚洲海域，英国东印度公司舰队于1762年10月自马德拉斯挥师占领西班牙统治下的马尼拉，吕宋岛北部的殖民秩序随之动摇。在伊洛科斯，驿使出身的迭戈·锡朗与妻子玛丽亚·何塞法·加布里埃拉——生于圣塔镇，父亲为西班牙裔伊洛卡诺人，母亲为山地伊特内格（廷吉安）人——驱逐贪虐的地方官员，废除强迫劳役与重税，在维甘建立自治政权。

1763年5月，教会与保皇派买通迭戈的旧友行刺身亡后，年仅三十二岁的加布里埃拉拒绝投降。她策马退入母亲族人聚居的阿布拉河谷山地皮迪甘，集结高地弓手与低地骑兵，于同年9月挥师反攻维甘；兵败被俘后，她与数十名义军同伴在维甘从容就义。

dateNote.en: 1731–1763 CE; led the Free Ilocos insurgency during the British occupation of Manila (1762–1763).
dateNote.zh: 1731—1763年；于英军占领马尼拉期间（1762—1763）参与并接掌伊洛科斯抗西起义。

title.en: Born in Santa, Ilocos Sur across lowland and Itneg worlds
title.zh: 生于南伊洛科斯圣塔镇，联结低地与伊特内格山地社群

description.en: Born 19 March 1731 in Barangay Caniogan, Santa, she grows up between coastal Ilocano parishes and her mother’s Itneg communities in the Abra mountains.
description.zh: 1731年3月19日生于圣塔镇，成长于沿海伊洛卡诺教区与母亲所属阿布拉山脉伊特内格族群的交界地带。

labelI18n.zh: 吕宋岛南伊洛科斯省圣塔镇

title.en: Joins Diego Silang’s Free Ilocos uprising at Vigan
title.zh: 在维甘投身迭戈·锡朗领导的“自由伊洛科斯”起义

description.en: Following the October 1762 British capture of Manila, Gabriela acts as advisor and field coordinator as Ilocano forces seize Vigan and abolish colonial tribute and forced labour.
description.zh: 1762年10月英军攻占马尼拉后，她担任起义军核心谋士与联络指挥，协助义军占领维甘并废除殖民贡税与强迫劳役。

labelI18n.zh: 南伊洛科斯省维甘

title.en: Regroups Itneg and Ilocano fighters in the Abra highlands
title.zh: 退守阿布拉高地皮迪甘重整伊特内格与伊洛卡诺义军

description.en: After Diego’s assassination on 28 May 1763, Gabriela retreats up the Abra River to Pidigan, uniting upland Itneg archers with lowland rebels under her command.
description.zh: 1763年5月28日迭戈遇刺后，她溯阿布拉河退入皮迪甘山区，亲自统率山地伊特内格弓手与低地义军。

labelI18n.zh: 吕宋岛阿布拉高地皮迪甘

title.en: Leads final assault on Vigan and is executed in September 1763
title.zh: 率军反攻维甘失利，于1763年9月被捕就义

description.en: Outnumbered by Spanish-led colonial levies during her September 1763 march on Vigan, she retreats toward Abra, is captured, and is publicly hanged at Vigan on 20 September 1763.
description.zh: 1763年9月率军攻打维甘时遭优势殖民征召军伏击，退往阿布拉途中被俘，9月20日在维甘慷慨就义。

title.en: Olaudah Equiano: mariner, Arctic explorer and abolitionist author
title.zh: 奥劳达·埃奎亚诺：买回自由、远航北极并书写废奴自传的水手

summary.en:
Enslaved in boyhood and renamed Gustavus Vassa by a Royal Navy officer, Olaudah Equiano hauled gunpowder under cannon fire at Louisbourg and Lagos during the Seven Years’ War before being sold without warning onto a Caribbean merchant estate in Montserrat. Working schooners between the West Indies, Philadelphia and Savannah, he traded glass tumblers, citrus and salted provisions on his own account until July 1766, when he laid down forty pounds sterling to purchase his manumission certificate.

Freedom took him even farther across the sea—including a 1773 Royal Navy polar expedition trapped in pack ice above Svalbard at 80° north. Settling in London, he joined fellow Black abolitionists in the Sons of Africa and in 1789 self-published *The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano*, touring Britain and Ireland through nine lifetime editions that turned personal maritime testimony into a weapon against the Atlantic slave trade.
summary.zh:
少年沦为奴隶并被英国皇家海军军官改名“古斯塔夫斯·瓦萨”的奥劳达·埃奎亚诺，曾在七年战争的路易斯堡与拉各斯海战炮火中搬运火药，却又在毫无预警下被转卖至加勒比海蒙特塞拉特岛的商庄。他随纵帆船往返西印度群岛、费城与萨凡纳之间，靠私下贩运玻璃杯、柑橘与腌货一点点攒钱，终于在1766年7月付清四十英镑赎身银，换得自由契书。

重获自由后，他继续远航四海——1773年更随英国极地探险舰队深入斯瓦尔巴群岛以北的北纬80度浮冰海域。定居伦敦后，他与黑人同道组建废奴团体“非洲之子”，并于1789年自费出版《奥劳达·埃奎亚诺生平奇事录》，亲赴英格兰、苏格兰与爱尔兰巡回宣讲，生前连印九版，以海上亲历证词重击跨大西洋奴隶贸易。

title.en: Mai of Raʻiātea: sailing to London to reclaim an occupied island home
title.zh: 赖阿特阿岛的迈伊：远航伦敦谋求光复故岛的太平洋旅人

labelI18n.zh: 社会群岛赖阿特阿岛与胡阿希内岛

summary.en:
When warriors from neighbouring Bora Bora invaded sacred Raʻiātea in the 1760s and killed his father, young Mai fled into exile on Tahiti and Huahine—wounded during Samuel Wallis’s 1767 bombardment at Matavai Bay yet calculating that British firearms might expel Raʻiātea’s occupiers. In September 1773 he boarded Tobias Furneaux’s HMS *Adventure*, becoming the first Pacific Islander to reach Britain.

In London between 1774 and 1776, sponsored by naturalist Joseph Banks, Mai was inoculated against smallpox, dined with Samuel Johnson, met King George III at Kew, and posed barefoot in flowing white barkcloth-like robes for Joshua Reynolds’s monumental canvas—with his Raʻiātean hand tattoos clearly visible. Returning aboard James Cook’s *Resolution* in 1777, he served as interpreter with Māori leaders at Totaranui in Aotearoa before settling on Huahine with horses, muskets and gifts that fell short of the alliance he had crossed two oceans to win.
summary.zh:
18世纪60年代，邻近波拉波拉岛的武士攻占圣岛赖阿特阿并杀害其父，年少的迈伊流亡大溪地与胡阿希内岛。1767年英国航海家沃利斯炮击马塔瓦伊湾时迈伊曾中弹负伤，但他敏锐意识到英国火器或许能助自己驱逐故岛的占领者。1773年9月，他主动登上弗诺指挥的皇家海军“探险号”，成为首位抵达不列颠的太平洋岛民。

1774至1776年居留伦敦期间，在博物学家约瑟夫·班克斯引介下，迈伊接种天花预防痘苗，与文学家塞缪尔·约翰逊共餐，在邱园觐见英王乔治三世，并赤足身披长袍、露出双手传统刺青，为约书亚·雷诺兹立像绘就巨幅油画。1777年他搭乘库克船长的“决心号”返航，途经新西兰托塔拉努伊湾时充任毛利首领的译员，最终携马匹与火枪定居胡阿希内岛，但跨越两大洋寻求的复岛同盟终未如愿。

dateNote.en: c. 1753 – c. 1779/1780 CE; sailed to Britain in 1773–1774, lived in England 1774–1776, and returned to Huahine in October 1777.

title.en: Munshi Abdullah: chronicling Melaka and Singapore in first-person Malay
title.zh: 文西阿都拉：以第一人称马来散文记录马六甲与新加坡巨变

location.label: Kampung Pali, Melaka, Straits of Malacca

labelI18n.en: Kampung Pali, Melaka, Straits of Malacca
labelI18n.zh: 马六甲海峡甘榜巴利（马六甲古城）

summary.en:
Growing up in polyglot Melaka in a Hadhrami Arab, Tamil Muslim and Malay scholarly family, Abdullah bin Abdul Kadir earned the title *Munshi* (language teacher) at eleven by tutoring Indian garrison soldiers in Quranic recitation and Malay. He copied classical Malay manuscripts for Stamford Raffles, mastered movable-type lithography with London Missionary Society printers, and moved back and forth to bustling new Singapore to teach Malay to Tamil, Chinese, British and American merchants.

Breaking away from courtly genealogies of kings and supernatural omens, his *Kisah Pelayaran Abdullah* (1838) and lithographed autobiography *Hikayat Abdullah* (completed 1843, published 1849) wrote in direct first-person Malay: mourning British demolition of Melaka’s ancient fort, exposing Singapore’s slave markets and triad violence, and urging Malay rulers to fund vernacular schools and printing presses. Setting sail on Hajj in 1854 with a travel diary in hand, he died of cholera shortly after reaching Mecca.
summary.zh:
生于多语交融的马六甲一个兼具哈德拉毛阿拉伯、泰米尔穆斯林与马来血统的书香之家，阿都拉·宾·阿都卡迪尔十一岁便因教驻防印度士兵诵经习字获称“文西”（导师）。他曾为莱佛士抄录马来古典写本，随伦敦传道会印工掌握石印与活字印刷术，并往返于新兴商埠新加坡，向泰米尔、华人与欧美商贾传授马来文。

突破传统宫廷谱系与神异叙事的成规，他在《阿都拉东海岸游记》（1838）与石印自传《阿都拉传》（1843年完稿、1849年印行）中改用鲜活的第一人称纪实马来散文：痛惜英军炸毁马六甲古堡城垣，直陈新加坡早期的奴隶贩卖与私会党械斗，并疾呼马来精英兴办母语学堂与印书馆。1854年他携日记登船赴麦加朝觐，抵圣城未久染霍乱辞世。

summary.en:
Born free in Salvador, Bahia, to Luiza Mahin—an African-born street vendor linked to the 1835 Malê Muslim slave uprising—and an impoverished Portuguese-descended father who illegally sold his own ten-year-old son to pay gambling debts, Luiz Gama arrived in chains at Rio de Janeiro and Santos in 1840. Taught to read and write at seventeen by a boarder in his master’s São Paulo house, Gama gathered proof of his free birth and walked out free in 1848.

Barred by race and class from enrolling officially at São Paulo’s Law Academy, he audited lectures in the corridors, read statutes in the library, and obtained a court license as a *rábula* (self-trained legal advocate). Turning Brazil’s own un-enforced 1831 anti-trafficking law against coffee planters, Gama won freedom suits for more than five hundred enslaved men, women and children, mocked pretentious imperial elites in his satirical poetry *Primeiras Trovas Burlescas* (1859), and saw huge crowds accompany his coffin through São Paulo six years before final abolition in 1888.
summary.zh:
生于巴伊亚州萨尔瓦多的自由民家庭——母亲路易莎·马欣是与1835年马莱穆斯林起义渊源深厚的非洲裔小贩，落魄的葡裔父亲却为偿赌债在1840年将年仅十岁的亲生儿子非法卖作奴隶。路易斯·伽马戴着镣铐经里约热内卢被贩往桑托斯与圣保罗；十七岁时随寄宿主人家中的学生习字读书，随后搜集自由出生证据，于1848年自行争回自由身。

因肤色与出身被圣保罗法学院拒之门外后，他在走廊旁听课程、泡在图书馆研读律例，考取“拉布拉”（自修讼师）出庭资格。他以巴西帝国长期束之高阁的1831年禁止输入非洲奴隶法为利刃，在法庭上迫使咖啡庄园主败诉，无偿为五百余名受奴役男女与孩童赢回自由，并以讽刺诗集《滑稽初吟》（1859）辛辣嘲弄帝国权贵的虚伪。1882年他在圣保罗病逝时数万人扶灵送葬；六年后，巴西终告废除奴隶制。

labelI18n.en: Parihaka kāinga beneath Mount Taranaki, Aotearoa New Zealand
labelI18n.zh: 新西兰北岛塔拉纳基山麓帕里哈卡村社

summary.en:
After colonial legislation confiscated more than a million acres across Taranaki during the New Zealand Wars of the 1860s, Te Whiti-o-Rongomai III of Te Ātiawa and Taranaki iwi gathered displaced families from across the country with his kinsman Tohu Kākahi at Parihaka, on the lower slopes of Mount Taranaki. Instead of building rifle pits, Parihaka grew into one of Aotearoa’s largest, best-fed settlements, wearing the white albatross feather (*raukura*) of peace.

When Crown surveyors began cutting roads across uncompensated Māori gardens in 1879, Te Whiti sent unarmed teams out to plough confiscated pastures and mend broken garden fences, calmly filling southern jails as hundreds submitted to arrest without striking a blow. On 5 November 1881, nearly 1,600 armed Constabulary and militia marched into Parihaka to find 2,000 villagers sitting quietly on the marae while skipping, singing children offered freshly baked loaves to the troops. Imprisoned without trial on the South Island until 1883, Te Whiti returned home to rebuild Parihaka with streetlights, piped water and monthly peace assemblies.
summary.zh:
19世纪60年代新西兰战争期间，殖民当局立法没收塔拉纳基逾百万英亩土地。出身特阿蒂阿瓦与塔拉纳基部族的特·菲蒂·奥·朗戈迈三世与族亲托胡·卡卡希在塔拉纳基山麓创建帕里哈卡村社，接纳各地流离失所的毛利家庭。他们没有修筑战壕枪垒，而是佩戴象征和平的信天翁白羽，将帕里哈卡建成当时新西兰规模最大、农产最丰足的聚落之一。

1879年殖民测量队强行穿过未获补偿的毛利菜园修路时，特·菲蒂派出手无寸铁的村民前往被没收的草场扶犁翻土、修补被毁的篱笆；数百人平静就捕、塞满南岛监狱，却未挥出一拳。1881年11月5日，近一千六百名武装警察与民兵开进帕里哈卡，迎面看到的却是两千余名静坐会场的村民，以及唱着歌、向士兵递上新烤面包的孩童。特·菲蒂未经审判被押往南岛羁押至1883年，获释归乡后又引入自来水与街灯重建帕里哈卡，每月召集和平集会直至辞世。

dateNote.en: Focused on his Parihaka leadership from c. 1866 through the 1879–1881 ploughing campaigns, South Island detention (1881–1883), and reconstruction until his death in November 1907.
dateNote.zh: 聚焦其自1860年代主持帕里哈卡村社、1879—1881年扶犁抗争、1881—1883年南岛羁押及返乡重建至1907年11月辞世的历程。

title.en: Cornelia Sorabji: storming Oxford law to advise secluded women across India
title.zh: 科妮莉亚·索拉布吉：闯入牛津法学考场、守护深闺妇女权益的印度女律师

location.label: Calcutta High Court and Court of Wards, Bengal, India

labelI18n.en: Calcutta High Court and Court of Wards, Bengal, India
labelI18n.zh: 印度孟加拉加尔各答高等法院与监护署

summary.en:
Born in Nashik in 1866 to Parsi-Christian educators Francina Ford and Sorabji Karsedji, Cornelia Sorabji watched secluded (*purdahnashin*) widows come to her mother’s door after losing inherited estates because custom forbade them to consult male lawyers—while colonial courts barred women from practicing law. Topping the Bombay Presidency as Deccan College’s first woman graduate yet denied a government scholarship on grounds of sex, she raised public subscriptions to enter Somerville Hall, Oxford, where special congregational decree allowed her in 1892 to become the first woman ever to sit Oxford’s Bachelor of Civil Law examinations.

Refused formal admission to the bar for another three decades, Sorabji returned to India, passed the Bombay LLB, and from 1904 travelled by palanquin, boat and train across Bengal, Bihar, Orissa and Assam as Lady Assistant to the Court of Wards—advising more than six hundred secluded women and orphans behind the curtain until women finally won the right to plead in Indian and British courts after 1919–1923.
summary.zh:
1866年生于纳西克一个帕西裔基督徒教育家家庭，科妮莉亚·索拉布吉自幼目睹深居帷幕（“普尔达”制度）的寡妇上门向她母亲求助：礼俗禁止她们面见男律师，殖民法庭又禁止女性执业，致使她们屡屡被人骗夺遗产。她以孟买管辖区头名成绩成为德干学院首位女毕业生，却因女性身份被拒发官费留英奖学金；随后在社会募捐支持下入读牛津萨默维尔学院，并于1892年经牛津特批成为史上首位参加民法学士考试的女性。

在长达三十余年被拒授予正式出庭资格的岁月里，索拉布吉返印考取孟买法学士，自1904年起乘轿、搭船、坐火车奔走于孟加拉、比哈尔、奥里萨与阿萨姆，任监护署女法律顾问，隔着帷幕为六百余名深闺妇孺清查地契、保全家产；直至1919—1923年间英印法律壁垒相继打破，她终获伦敦林肯律师学院与加尔各答高等法院正式大律师资格。
